title: Checkpointed Fragment Handshake and Seal Protocol for Streaming Structured JSON
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Problem: Streaming structured JSON with interleaved tool/function calls frequently suffers from partial fragments, escape-state ambiguities, and truncation at arbitrary token boundaries. Existing repair heuristics (heuristic reassembly, sentinel insertion) work in many cases but yield non-deterministic outcomes across SDK versions and can cause duplicated or partial tool invocations. Goal: Define and implement a lightweight, wire-compatible protocol that provides deterministic fragment checkpoints, an escape-transparent handshake for tool-call boundaries, and an idempotent replay/seal mechanism so clients and servers can recover safely across truncation/reconnects without duplicating side-effects.
technical_design: Overview: introduce a Checkpointed Fragment Handshake (CFH) and Seal format appended to streamed frames. Key concepts: 1) Fragment sequence numbers (fsn): monotonic per-stream integers embedded in frame metadata. 2) Escape state snapshot: compact bitmask + last-escape-byte to capture partial multi-byte escape sequences so downstream parsers can re-enter the same escape state. 3) Truncation hint token: lightweight marker indicating the stream ended mid-token and the token-safety offset. 4) Seal/receipt: server-issued idempotent receipt for any fragment that completes a tool-call boundary; receipts include fsn range, checksum, and tool-call idempotency token. 5) Version negotiation: wire-protocol version in initial frame; clients that don't support CFH fall back to legacy sentinel-mode with server-side best-effort repair. Handshake flow (happy path): - Client opens streaming session, includes protocol_version=2 in first frame. - Server replies acknowledging CFH and returns starting fsn. - As model generates, frames include fsn, escape_snapshot, and optional truncation_hint. - When the model completes a tool-call or structured object boundary, server emits a seal with receipt. - Client persists last-seen receipt; on reconnect it requests replay from receipt.fsn+1. Replay semantics and idempotency: receipts include a server-signed idempotency token; tool-call adapters must accept token to deduplicate side effects. Compatibility shim: clients with protocol_version=1 receive frames with extra sentinel markers so older SDKs can still reassemble, and server will keep the legacy repair layer for at most 7 days post-upgrade before requiring CFH. Implementation notes: - Use compact binary metadata (base64 in JSON payloads) to avoid increasing CPU on existing path. - Checksum: CRC32c over frame payload + metadata. - Limit replay window to configurable max_replay_span (default 10k tokens) to bound memory. - Provide SDK helpers for escape_snapshot application and receipt verification.
acceptance_criteria: Server emits fsn+escape_snapshot metadata for streamed frames when protocol_version>=2
Server issues 'seal' receipts for completed tool-call boundaries containing checksum and idempotency token
Client SDK can reconnect and request replay from last-seen receipt and rehydrate the structured output deterministically
Backwards compatibility: legacy clients (protocol_version=1) still receive sentinel-framed streams and experience no regressions
E2E test demonstrating no duplicated tool-side effects when replaying after network disconnects
implementation_plan: 1) Add wire-protocol version header to streaming open frame (server + Rust runtime) - 3d
2) Implement fsn counters and attach compact metadata (escape snapshot, truncation hint) to stream frames - 5d
3) Create server seal generator that emits receipts at tool-call/object boundaries and persists last-sealed fsn - 3d
4) SDK changes (JS, Python, Go): add applyEscapeSnapshot and replay-from-receipt helpers - 5d
5) Tool-adapter change: accept idempotency token header on tool invocation to deduplicate - 2d
6) Compatibility shim: maintain sentinel-mode path and add version-negotiation tests - 3d
7) Integration tests and chaos testing (disconnects during escape sequences, abrupt truncations) - 5d
8) Rollout plan and gradual enablement via feature flag - 2d
test_plan: Unit: escape_snapshot encode/decode round trips (edge escape bytes, multibyte sequences)
Integration: simulate reconnect at N different fsn positions and verify replayed stream is bit-identical after applying receipts
Property: fuzz truncated streams across token boundaries and ensure no malformed JSON passes through structured-output validator
E2E: tool-call adapter receives idempotency token and returns unique marker; after replay, assert only one side-effect recorded
Backward-compat: test protocol_version=1 clients against upgraded server for 72h smoke tests
rollout_plan: Alpha: internal experiments with Redwood Console and SDK internal builds (week 1)
Beta: opt-in feature flag for selected customers (week 2-3)
Canary: region-limited rollout with telemetry gates (week 4)
General availability after 2 weeks of stable canary and no high-severity regressions
monitoring_metrics: checkpointed_frames_percent: percent of frames that include CFH metadata
seal_issue_rate: number of seals emitted per 1k tokens
replay_success_rate: percent of reconnects that successfully replay and rehydrate structured output
duplicate_tool_invocations: count of dedup failures (tool adapters returning duplicate side-effects)
avg_recovery_latency_ms: time from reconnect to successful rehydrate
progress_updates: 2026-03-02: Spike complete. Evaluated escape state encodings; selected 2-byte compact snapshot format.
2026-03-05: Prototype server emits fsn metadata; initial SDK helpers drafted in JS.
2026-03-10: Tool-adapter idempotency header prototype merged into internal toolbridge service.
2026-03-13: Design review with reliability and SDK teams; feedback captured and incorporated into test_plan
blockers: Tool vendor adapters must accept idempotency token; some third-party connectors need updates
Decision pending on max_replay_span default value for Dedicated customers (cost/retention tradeoff)
